IT & INFORMATION SECURITY POLICIES
Enterprise Data Protection, Encryption & Classification
Policy
Classification Matrix, Cryptographic Standards, Retention, and Media Disposal
Classification: Confidential
Version: 3.2
Owner: Data Governance & Privacy
Standard: GDPR / ISO 27001
1. Objective and Compliance Baseline
The Enterprise Data Protection Policy establishes standards for data classification, cryptographic protection, retention,
and secure disposal across Apex Global Technologies. This policy ensures strict compliance with the EU General Data
Protection Regulation (GDPR), California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA), and SOC 2 Type II confidentiality
requirements.

3. Cryptographic Standards (Encryption at Rest and in Transit)
Encryption at Rest: All databases (PostgreSQL, Redis), Amazon EBS volumes, S3 buckets, and backup archives
must be encrypted using AES-256. Endpoint laptops must enforce full-disk encryption (Apple FileVault 2 on macOS,
BitLocker with TPM 2.0 on Windows).
Encryption in Transit: All data transmitted over internal or external networks must use TLS 1.3 (with TLS 1.2
permitted as a legacy fallback). Cleartext protocols (HTTP, Telnet, FTP) are blocked at the perimeter firewall.
4. Data Retention, Archival, and Sanitization
Retention Schedules: Operational application logs are retained for 90 days in hot storage and archived for 365 days
in cold storage (AWS S3 Glacier). Customer datasets are deleted within 30 days of contract termination.
Media Sanitization: Decommissioned hardware storage devices must undergo cryptographic erasure complying with 
NIST SP 800-88 Revision 1 (Guidelines for Media Sanitization) or physical degaussing and shredding with a
Certificate of Destruction.
